ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the attached figure, four aromatic compounds with substituents are labeled A, B, C, D in order. On the benzene ring of A there is –CHO attached; on the benzene ring of B there is –OCH3 attached; on the benzene ring of C there is –Cl attached; on the benzene ring of D there is –NO2 attached. It should be noted that the options listed in the question text are inconsistent with the labels in the attached figure; judging according to the attached figure options, B corresponds to methoxybenzene/anisole, not the benzoic acid in the text. Then reason: the question asks whether the electrophilic substitution reaction rate is faster than benzene. –CHO, –Cl, and –NO2 all overall have a deactivating effect on the benzene ring, making the electrophilic substitution reaction slower than benzene; –OCH3 can activate the benzene ring by donating electrons through resonance, making the electrophilic substitution reaction faster than benzene. Therefore, according to the attached figure labels, only B is faster than benzene.

method.method_draft: After identifying the image structures, compare how each substituent affects the rate-determining arenium-ion formation. For B, the methoxy oxygen can donate electron density into the aromatic ring and stabilize the cationic intermediate, so the ring reacts faster than benzene. raw_record.original_question:
下列哪种物质的亲电取代反应速率比苯更快?
A. $\ce{C6H5NO2}$ (硝基苯)
B. $\ce{C6H5COOH}$ (苯甲酸)
C. $\ce{C6H5Cl}$ (氯苯)
D. $\ce{C6H5NH2}$ (苯胺)
raw_record.final_cot: First describe the image: in the attached figure, four aromatic compounds with substituents are labeled A, B, C, D in order. On the benzene ring of A there is –CHO attached; on the benzene ring of B there is –OCH3 attached; on the benzene ring of C there is –Cl attached; on the benzene ring of D there is –NO2 attached. It should be noted that the options listed in the question text are inconsistent with the labels in the attached figure; judging according to the attached figure options, B corresponds to methoxybenzene/anisole, not the benzoic acid in the text. Then reason: the question asks whether the electrophilic substitution reaction rate is faster than benzene. –CHO, –Cl, and –NO2 all overall have a deactivating effect on the benzene ring, making the electrophilic substitution reaction slower than benzene; –OCH3 can activate the benzene ring by donating electrons through resonance, making the electrophilic substitution reaction faster than benzene. Therefore, according to the attached figure labels, only B is faster than benzene.
